```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

Step 3 of the fishing-activity flow puts the gear on the track: which
gear was used, and — for towed gear — how wide it was, since gear width
is what turns track into swept area. The ICES VMS datacall asks for
gear width by métier, and the standard source is the BENTHIS model:
gear width as a function of gear group and vessel size (length or
power), linear or a power function.

```{r}
library(ramb)
library(dplyr)
```

## Métier codes

ICES logbook records carry level-6 métier codes such as
`OTB_DEF_>=120_0_0` (gear, target assemblage, mesh size range, ...).
`rb_extract_metier()` pulls out a part:

```{r}
codes <- c("OTB_DEF_>=120_0_0", "GNS_DEF_60-79_0_0", "DRB_MOL_0_0_0",
           "SDN_DEF_>=120_0_0", "OTB_CRU_70-89_0_0")

rb_extract_metier(codes, part = "gear")
rb_extract_metier(codes, part = "metier5")
```

The full ICES vocabularies (gears, target assemblages, métier levels 5
and 6) are available through `rb_get_gear_vocabulary()`, which fetches
them with {icesVocab}. The mapping from métier level 5 to the 14
BENTHIS gear groups is shipped with the package:

```{r}
metier5_benthis_lookup
```

## The BENTHIS parameters

For each BENTHIS métier, `benthis_parameters` holds the coefficients of
the vessel size–gear width relationship: a linear model
(`width = a * size + b`) or a power model (`width = a * size^b`), with
vessel size measured as length overall (`avg_oal`) or engine power
(`avg_kw`), depending on the métier:

```{r}
benthis_parameters |>
  select(benthis_metier, a, b, model, variable)
```

## Predicting gear width

`rb_predict_gear_width()` wraps the lookup and the two model forms.
Given a small fleet — métier, length and engine power per vessel:

```{r}
fleet <-
  tibble::tribble(
    ~metier6,             ~length, ~kw,
    "OTB_DEF_>=120_0_0",      24,   447,
    "OTB_DEF_70-89_0_0",      18,   220,
    "GNS_DEF_60-79_0_0",      12,    96,
    "DRB_MOL_0_0_0",          15,   130,
    "SDN_DEF_>=120_0_0",      32,   735,
    "OTB_CRU_70-89_0_0",      21,   330
  )

fleet |>
  mutate(metier5 = rb_extract_metier(metier6, part = "metier5"),
         width = rb_predict_gear_width(metier5, length, kw))
```

Static gear (here the gillnet métier `GNS_DEF`) has no BENTHIS width —
swept area is a towed-gear concept — and comes back `NA`.

The function returns metres; divide by 1000 if your workflow expects
kilometres (the ICES VMS datacall flow does).

Under the hood this is exactly:

```{r}
fleet |>
  mutate(metier5 = rb_extract_metier(metier6, part = "metier5")) |>
  left_join(metier5_benthis_lookup, by = join_by(metier5)) |>
  left_join(benthis_parameters |> select(benthis_metier:variable),
            by = join_by(benthis_metier)) |>
  mutate(width =
           case_when(
             model == "power"  & variable == "avg_kw"  ~ a * kw^b,
             model == "power"  & variable == "avg_oal" ~ a * length^b,
             model == "linear" & variable == "avg_oal" ~ a * length + b,
             .default = NA)) |>
  pull(width)
```

written out as a pipe — useful when you need the intermediate columns
(e.g. to carry `subsurface_percentage` for penetration estimates).
